sourceRef.section: Appendix M — Optional Dice Tables and Randomized Card Selection

title: Optional Dice Tables and Randomized Card Selection
version: Campaign Mode v4.4 — Consolidated Dice Reference
overview: This appendix provides optional methods for replacing randomized campaign card draws with ordinary six-sided dice.
These methods apply to randomized campaign components such as Agendas, Political Task selection, Neutral Opportunities, Discoveries, and Development rewards.
They do not replace the strategic selection of Company Orders or Faction Maneuver cards. Players and the GM still choose those cards according to the normal campaign rules.

methods.name: Exact Positional 2D6
description: Use two distinguishable D6 to generate a uniformly distributed result from 1 to 36.
This method can select from a numbered list of up to 36 remaining entries.
It supports exact draws without replacement.
Use this method when preserving the physical deck's depletion and probabilities matters.

methods.name: Quick 2D6 Tables
description: Roll two D6 and add their values.
Quick tables deliberately assign more common results to more numerous reward categories.
These tables are convenient but ordinarily represent draws with replacement, unless additional tracking is used.

M1_diceRandomizationMethods.recommendedDefault: Use Exact Positional 2D6 for Task selection, Discoveries, and unique cards. Use the Quick Development table when simplified reward generation is preferred.

procedure: Use two distinguishable D6. Designate one die as A and the other as B.
Roll both dice and calculate: R = 6 × (A − 1) + B.
This generates an equally likely integer from 1 to 36. Every result has an equal 1-in-36 probability.

quickPositionalTable.description: R for each (A, B) combination. Columns are Die B (1–6), rows are Die A (1–6).

notes: This is an ordered roll.
Rolling A = 2 and B = 5 produces 11.
Rolling A = 5 and B = 2 produces 26.
The two results are different.

sourceRef.section: M.3 Drawing from a Numbered List

M3_drawingFromANumberedList.setup: Suppose a deck or eligible pool contains N remaining entries, where N is between 1 and 36. Number the remaining entries from 1 to N.

steps.name: Determine the Acceptance Limit
steps.formula: L = N × (36 ÷ N, rounded down to a whole number)

steps.name: Roll
steps.procedure: Generate R using Exact Positional 2D6. If R is greater than L, reroll both dice.

steps.name: Determine the Selected Entry
steps.effect: Select entry I. Every remaining entry has the same probability of being selected.

steps.name: Remove the Selected Entry
steps.procedure: For a draw without replacement, remove the selected entry from the numbered list. Renumber the remaining entries from 1 to N−1. Use the same procedure for the next draw. If the draw's rules return the selected entry to the pool, retain it instead.

M3_drawingFromANumberedList.note: For one or two remaining entries, the same method works without rejection.

sourceRef.section: M.4 Example — Drawing from Seven Tasks

worked: A Standard Campaign Act uses seven Task cards, numbered 1–7.
The acceptance limit is: L = 7 × (36 ÷ 7, rounded down) = 7 × 5 = 35.
The GM rolls A = 6 and B = 6. This generates R = 36. Because 36 exceeds 35, reroll.
The next roll is A = 3 and B = 5. R = 6 × (3 − 1) + 5 = 17.
The selected index is: I = 1 + ((17 − 1) mod 7) = 3. Select Task 3.
Remove it from the available list. Six Tasks remain.
The next draw uses N = 6, which requires no rejection.

M5_randomizingActAgendas.setup: Each Act has exactly three possible Agendas. Roll one D6.
notes: Each Agenda has an equal one-third chance of selection.
The two unselected Agendas are not used during that Act.
knownIssues: Agenda names here (e.g. 'Whispers of War', 'Broken Accord') do not match the names used for the Act Agendas transcribed in campaign/03_act_agendas.json (Appendix C), which uses different Agenda identifiers/themes per Act. This is flagged as an inter-appendix inconsistency rather than resolved, since both are direct transcriptions of their respective source appendices.

taskPoolProcedure: Prepare the eligible Open Task list.
Prepare the eligible Sponsored Task list.
Prepare the eligible Exclusive Task list.
Remove Tasks that cannot legally apply to the campaign.
Use Exact Positional 2D6 to select the required number from each classification.
Remove selected Tasks from their respective eligible lists.
Combine the selected Tasks into the Act pool.
Reveal the first three to form the Task Display.
M6_randomizingPoliticalTaskPools.refreshRule: When the Active Task resolves, remove it and reveal the next Task from the Act pool. The GM may use the positional method to select among the remaining Act-pool entries rather than physically shuffling the selected Tasks.
importantRestrictions: Only Tasks associated with participating Grand Factions are eligible.
Do not use this procedure to select the Active Stake itself.
The Council Influence holder chooses the Active Stake from the available Task Display.
Task randomization determines what becomes available, not what the PCs or GM choose to pursue.

M7_schedulingNeutralOpportunities.setup: Every Act contains one Treasury Opportunity. Additional Special Opportunities depend on campaign length.
schedulingProcedure: Number the Turns within the Act.
Randomly select one Turn for the Treasury Opportunity.
Remove that Turn from the available schedule.
Randomly select each required Special Opportunity Turn from the remaining Turns.
notes: Use Exact Positional 2D6 when the number of eligible Turns is greater than six.
No Turn receives two scheduled Neutral Opportunities under the normal procedure.

selectingTreasuryCards.cards: There are four Treasury cards, numbered F-T1 through F-T4.
selectingTreasuryCards.method: Use the positional method with N = 4, or roll a D6 and reroll 5–6.
selectingTreasuryCards.drawRule: Draw without replacement across the campaign until the four Treasury cards have been used.
selectingTreasuryCards.reward: Every Treasury Opportunity provides the same reward: 2 Gold per PC. The card determines the objective's narrative form.

selectingSpecialCards.cards: There are eight Special Opportunity cards, numbered F-S1 through F-S8.
selectingSpecialCards.method: Use Exact Positional 2D6 with N = 8. Accept results 1–32. Reroll 33–36. Select one of the eight entries uniformly.
selectingSpecialCards.drawRule: Remove that card from the remaining Special Opportunity catalog.

usageByCampaignLength.specialCardsUsed: All eight Special cards across its four Acts.
Normally four of the eight Special cards.

procedure: The Discovery deck contains twelve unique cards, numbered G-D1 through G-D12.
For the first Discovery draw, use N = 12. All thirty-six positional 2D6 outcomes are accepted. Each Discovery has probability 1/12.
After selecting the card, remove it from the available list. The next draw uses N = 11. Continue adjusting N as cards are removed.

exploreSupremacy.context: When Explore Supremacy permits revealing two Discoveries:
steps: Draw the first card using the current eligible pool.
Draw a second card from the remaining pool.
Return the unchosen card to the eligible pool.
notes: This produces two distinct eligible rewards.
If only one Discovery remains, resolve it normally.
The GM should not use two independent rolls that might select the same unique card when the effect specifically requires revealing two different cards.

M8_1_fastTwelveDiscoveryLookup.applicability: For the initial complete Discovery pool only; players may use a simpler equally likely 2D6 lookup. The first die selects the left group when odd and the right group when even; the second die selects the row. This is an alternative to the positional calculation, not an additional draw.
notes: Each card has probability 1/12 on the first draw.

For subsequent draws, either reroll results corresponding to removed cards or use the exact positional method among the remaining eligible entries. Rerolling used cards reproduces drawing without replacement while at least one remains eligible.
Do not substitute the older 'Hidden Settlement' card; the current twelfth Discovery is 'The Hidden Waystone'.

M9_exactDevelopmentRewardDraws.setup: The Development deck contains eighteen physical cards. Number all eighteen individual copies, including repeated copies of the same reward.
procedure: Use Exact Positional 2D6 with N = 18. Each individual entry is equally likely.
When a reward is drawn, remove that copy from the remaining list.
Keep held temporary rewards unavailable to the draw pool until used, discarded, or expired.
When the draw pool becomes empty, recycle the eligible discard pool according to Appendix H.
example: Suppose the dice show: A = 5, B = 2.
Entry 8 is Windfall. The PC Company gains 2 Gold.
Remove that copy of Windfall from the available Development list. The next draw uses the remaining seventeen entries.
This procedure exactly reproduces physical card draws without replacement.

M10_quickDevelopmentRewardTable.basis: This table uses the ordinary sum of 2D6, not positional 2D6. It represents the current 18-card Appendix H deck with War Chest = 1 Gold and Windfall = 2 Gold.
M10_quickDevelopmentRewardTable.purpose: Designed so that the probability of each Development category exactly matches its initial proportion in the eighteen-card deck. It is an optional with-replacement alternative, not a substitute for tracking held or spent cards when finite-deck behavior matters.
M10_quickDevelopmentRewardTable.note: These are precisely the proportions of the eighteen-card Development deck before any cards are removed.

expectedGoldValue.basis: War Chest contributes 1 Gold, and Windfall contributes 2 Gold. Other Development rewards are not included in this direct Gold expectation.

importantLimitation: The Quick Development table reproduces the deck's initial category probabilities, but does not automatically reproduce its changing composition after cards have been drawn.
Repeated 2D6 sum rolls allow the same reward category to appear indefinitely.
Use the Quick table for a simplified with-replacement reward system.
Use Exact Positional 2D6 with a remaining-card list for exact no-replacement draws.
Do not claim the Quick table reproduces physical deck depletion without maintaining and adjusting the remaining category probabilities.

M11_randomizingOtherSmallLists.applicability: The positional method may also be used for a list of legal, equally appropriate alternatives.
examples: Selecting a random unresolved Site from a list.
Determining which of several equally suitable locations receives an incidental event.
Selecting among equally plausible minor complications.
notes: Always identify the legal list before rolling.
The result cannot select an ineligible action or unavailable target.
The exact positional method is valid for list sizes up to thirty-six.
For larger lists, divide the entries into suitable subsets or use an appropriate larger randomizer.

M12_whenNotToRoll.principle: Do not randomize decisions that belong to players, the GM, or established faction interests.

intentionalChoices.controlledBy: Council Influence holder or valid Political Mandate

notes: The purpose of optional dice tables is to replace randomized deck draws, not remove strategic agency.
Independent faction decisions may use a fair random selection only when several legal options remain genuinely equivalent after applying the faction's established priorities.

table.recommendedMethod: Positional 2D6, or fast odd/even lookup with rejection
Positional 2D6, N = remaining physical card copies

coreFormulas.rerollRule: Reroll results above the highest multiple of N that does not exceed 36.

closingNote: End of Appendix M — consolidated from the two prior Appendix M drafts.
